protocol: Record actual onset/last-known-well, deficit, examination times, prior treatment and comparison; identify every NCCT, CTA/MRA, perfusion, MRI or venographic component actually acquired with coverage and quality.

Review NCCT for haemorrhage and parenchymal change; review actual arch-to-vertex vascular coverage/phase and each target segment. MRI requires DWI with ADC, FLAIR and susceptibility as acquired. Venous suspicion requires appropriate actual venographic assessment rather than dense blood alone.

Check source perfusion motion, bolus, temporal sampling, truncation, coverage and processing before using estimates. Protocol/order and selection imaging follow the current clinical pathway and should avoid unnecessary reperfusion delay.

checklist.label: Haemorrhage
checklist.detail: Assess each actually acquired parenchymal, subarachnoid, ventricular and extra-axial bleeding compartment, side/site and extent; distinguish haemorrhagic transformation and unassessed limits.

checklist.label: Parenchyma
checklist.detail: Localise each acute or uncertain change by side, actual structure and vascular or venous distribution; describe applicable modality-specific MCA ASPECTS regions and separate prior injury or artefact.

checklist.label: Occlusion
checklist.detail: Assess each actually acquired arterial segment, occlusion extent, reconstitution, tandem cervical disease, stenosis/dissection and variants; assess venous findings on appropriate venography when acquired.

checklist.label: Collaterals
checklist.detail: Describe actual acquisition phases, collateral spatial extent and relative delay; retain coverage/flow/processing limitations before describing software-defined perfusion estimates.

checklist.label: Tissue and complications
checklist.detail: Assess each actual injury/estimated tissue region, oedema, shift, cisterns, ventricular obstruction, herniation, comparison and alternative diagnosis without inferring viability or current-patient findings from source examples.

measurements.name: ASPECTS
measurements.method: On an applicable MCA-territory source examination record CT or DWI modality, side, each of the ten assessed regions and acute change; score 10 minus affected regions. Retain old lesions, artefacts and unassessed regions.
measurements.pitfall: MCA ASPECTS is not a posterior circulation score, exact core volume, tissue viability assay or independent treatment rule.

measurements.name: Perfusion volumes
measurements.method: Only when acquisition/processing is adequate, record software/version, thresholds/units, estimated core and delayed region volumes in mL, mismatch volume and ratio with actual scope and uncertainty.
measurements.pitfall: Static colour maps are not numerical source maps. Motion, bolus, delay, truncation, coverage and platform effects can invalidate estimates; predicted core does not mean wholly irreversible tissue.

measurements.name: Vascular calibre and extent
measurements.method: Name the actual vessel/segment, proximal/distal lesion extent, native calibrated measurement plane, stenosis convention/reference vessel and luminal/wall findings actually resolved.
measurements.pitfall: Do not infer vessel patency from missing acquisition, a generic mesh, a dense vessel or apparent absence on a single phase. Flow, bolus and variant anatomy can mimic occlusion.

measurements.name: Midline shift and ventricular effect
measurements.method: Measure current-study shift in mm with direction, stated anatomical level and ideal-midline method; assess each acquired ventricular/cisternal compartment and obstruction/effacement.
measurements.pitfall: Selected publication slices do not establish complete extent, patient calibration, a current shift measurement or hydrocephalus.

classification.name: ASPECTS
classification.version: Ten-region MCA assessment; specify NCCT or DWI application
classification.applicability: An applicable MCA-territory examination, with actual side, regions and acquisition stated.
classification.summary: Name each affected and unassessed region with the score; keep posterior circulation and perfusion separate. Treatment selection uses the actual clinical pathway.

pitfalls: Normal early CT or an initially negative DWI does not exclude clinically consistent stroke; small/posterior lesions and acquisition limits require context.
DWI/ADC/FLAIR evolution varies. DWI–FLAIR mismatch is selection context, not an exact onset clock or an automatic treatment decision.
Predicted core and delayed tissue are imaging/processing estimates; low CBF, diffusion restriction and hypoattenuation do not prove wholly irreversible tissue.
Single-phase CTA can miss delayed filling. Collateral status does not justify avoidable delay or independently exclude reperfusion assessment.
Arterial and venous infarction can both be haemorrhagic. Dense sinus or nonterritorial injury raises a venous question; actual CTV/MRV and the clinical pathway establish the assessment.
Source cases, next-day DWI, motion/reprocessing plots and separate source patients are teaching context. They neither register to one another nor autofill the current patient report.
impression_prompts: State each actual haemorrhage or ischaemic/uncertain lesion with side/site, extent and acquisition limitations.
State each actual target arterial or venous finding, tissue/collateral estimates and urgent complication; distinguish acquired findings from unassessed questions.
Communicate the actual time-sensitive imaging question to the stroke team using current clinical/time/imaging eligibility; source scores or estimates alone do not determine treatment.
escalation: Promptly communicate acute haemorrhage, target-vessel occlusion, suspected significant venous thrombosis or threatening oedema/herniation with actual finding, limits, recipient and time.
